Alex / Camila — quick technical notes on batching / concurrency that should help when you complete the worksheet: 

1) Continuous batching model: if your traffic is a fairly steady stream (we typically see >50% of requests arriving within a rolling 100–500ms window), our runtime can form micro-batches that substantially reduce per-token compute. For a low-latency workload this often yields an effective batching factor of ~3–6 depending on arrival jitter and request-length variance.

2) Concurrency sizing: for interactive requests with p95 latency targets, we size targets on concurrent streams (rps * avg latency). Example: 50 rps with avg 200ms token generation -> ~10 concurrent in-flight streams. For background summarization (async), you can queue and batch aggressively.

3) Unit economics (very rough, depends on chosen model/quantization):
- Hosted baseline for mid-sized open model (e.g., Llama-like, fp16/quant) — ballpark $120–$300 per 1M tokens.
- With continuous batching and prefix caching for stable sessions you often see 20–40% cost reductions vs naive single-request serving.
- If you can tolerate 8-bit quantization + continuous batching we can push toward the lower end (~$100–$150/1M) in a pilot.

4) Data points we'd need from you for precise pricing: avg tokens per request (in+out), % of long-form summaries (>512 tokens), peak qps and expected sustained qps.

I'll also include a short note in the MAP about recommended concurrency & batching settings for the pilot cluster.

— Aditya
